_comment: Agent rows for the 34 IARC Monograph chemicals that appear in suppl_data/filtered_table.csv but not in data.js. CAS / IARC group / monograph volume verified against IARC Monographs Vols 107–128. Loaded with source='kcad' on the AgentReference table; the Agent table has no provenance column yet, so these rows are indistinguishable from curator-added agents — that's intentional, they become first-class agents that human curators can extend.

agents.name: 1,3-Propane sultone
agents.summary: Bifunctional alkylating agent; chain-transfer reagent for surfactants and battery electrolytes. Forms DNA adducts and acts as a direct mutagen.

agents.name: 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D)
agents.summary: Auxin-mimetic broadleaf herbicide; one of the most widely used selective herbicides since the 1940s. Inconclusive cancer evidence in humans; positive in some occupational cohorts.

agents.name: 2-Mercaptobenzothiazole
agents.summary: Vulcanisation accelerator used in rubber manufacture; documented occupational bladder-cancer signal in vulcanisation workers.

agents.name: 3,3',4,4'-Tetrachloroazobenzene (TCAB)
agents.summary: Dioxin-like contaminant of 3,4-dichloroaniline-based herbicides. Potent aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) agonist.

agents.name: 4,4'-Methylene-bis(2-chloroaniline) (MOCA)
agents.summary: Curing agent for cast polyurethane elastomers; metabolised to electrophilic intermediates that form DNA adducts. Sufficient evidence for urinary-bladder cancer in humans.

agents.name: Acrolein
agents.summary: Highly reactive α,β-unsaturated aldehyde present in tobacco smoke and combustion emissions. Forms Michael adducts on DNA bases and proteins.

agents.name: Aldrin
agents.summary: Organochlorine insecticide rapidly epoxidised in vivo to dieldrin. Banned in most countries; persistent in food chains.

agents.name: Aldrin / Dieldrin (mixture)
agents.summary: Joint annotation used in KCAD for studies treating Aldrin and its in-vivo metabolite Dieldrin as a single exposure.

agents.name: Aniline
agents.summary: Aromatic amine used as a dye and polymer precursor. Activated by N-hydroxylation; classic example of aromatic-amine carcinogenesis.

agents.name: Aniline hydrochloride
agents.summary: Salt form of aniline used in industrial settings; same toxicodynamics as the free base.

agents.name: Carbon nanotubes (MWCNT-7)
agents.summary: Multi-walled carbon nanotubes; Group 2B applies specifically to MWCNT-7. Mechanically and inflammation-driven mesothelial carcinogenesis akin to asbestos.

agents.name: DDT
agents.summary: Persistent organochlorine insecticide; first widespread synthetic pesticide. Reclassified to 2A in 2015 on the basis of liver, testicular and NHL evidence.

agents.name: Diazinon
agents.summary: Organophosphate insecticide; metabolised to diazoxon, a cholinesterase inhibitor with genotoxic side activity.

agents.name: Dichloromethane
agents.summary: Methylene chloride; widely used as paint stripper and process solvent. Metabolised by GSTT1 to genotoxic intermediates.

agents.name: Dieldrin
agents.summary: Persistent organochlorine; epoxide metabolite of aldrin. Inadequate evidence in humans despite extensive bioactivity data.

agents.name: Glycidol
agents.summary: Reactive epoxy-alcohol used in epoxide synthesis and sterilisation. Forms DNA adducts in multiple tissues.

agents.name: Glycidyl methacrylate
agents.summary: Bi-functional monomer combining a glycidyl epoxide and a methacrylate vinyl group. Direct genotoxin in standard assays.

agents.name: Hydrazine
agents.summary: Powerful reducing agent used in rocket fuels and boiler-water treatment. Forms methyl-DNA adducts via in-vivo methylation.

agents.name: Hydrazine sulfate
agents.summary: Salt form of hydrazine used in agricultural and pharmaceutical synthesis; same toxicodynamics as hydrazine.

agents.name: Lindane
agents.summary: γ-Hexachlorocyclohexane; organochlorine insecticide and scabicide. Reclassified to Group 1 in 2015 on the basis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma evidence.

agents.name: Malathion
agents.summary: Organophosphate; activated to malaoxon, a cholinesterase inhibitor with genotoxic activity at high doses.

agents.name: N,N-Dimethylformamide
agents.summary: Polar aprotic solvent widely used in pharmaceutical, polymer and acrylic-fibre manufacturing. Hepatotoxic; testicular and HCC signals in cohorts.

agents.name: Nitroanisole
agents.summary: Generic KCAD label for nitroanisole isomers; see also ortho-nitroanisole for the IARC-listed compound.

agents.name: Parathion
agents.summary: Highly toxic organophosphate, banned in most countries. Activated to paraoxon; mechanism-of-action data link it to oxidative stress and immunosuppression.

agents.name: Pentachlorophenol
agents.summary: Wood preservative and biocide. Sufficient evidence for non-Hodgkin lymphoma and soft-tissue sarcoma in occupational cohorts.

agents.name: Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs)
agents.summary: Mixture of 209 congeners formerly used as dielectric fluids; bioaccumulative. AhR-mediated promotion plus immunotoxicity; sufficient evidence for melanoma in humans.

agents.name: Styrene
agents.summary: Monomer for polystyrene and ABS resins; activated to genotoxic styrene-7,8-oxide by CYP2E1/2B6.

agents.name: Styrene + Styrene-7,8-oxide (mixture)
agents.summary: Joint annotation for KCAD studies that report effects of styrene and its primary genotoxic metabolite together.

agents.name: Styrene-7,8-oxide
agents.summary: Reactive epoxide metabolite of styrene; direct genotoxin forming DNA and haemoglobin adducts.

agents.name: Styrene oxide
agents.summary: Alternative KCAD label for styrene-7,8-oxide; same CAS.

agents.name: Tetrabromobisphenol A (TBBPA)
agents.summary: Most-used reactive brominated flame retardant; endocrine-active and thyroid-axis disruptor.

agents.name: ortho-Anisidine hydrochloride
agents.summary: Salt form of ortho-anisidine used in dye manufacture; same activation pathway as the free base.

agents.name: ortho-Anisidine
agents.summary: Methoxylated aromatic amine used in azo dye synthesis. N-hydroxylated to electrophilic nitrenium ion; urinary-bladder carcinogen in animals.

agents.name: ortho-Nitroanisole
agents.summary: Aromatic nitro-ether used as a dye and pharmaceutical intermediate; reduced to ortho-anisidine in vivo.
